title: AI/ML Questions bank question
description: A multiple-choice question. Each file in questions/ is a list of these objects. Texts are maps by language: English is required and Spanish optional; if Spanish is missing, the site shows the English text.

id.description: <area>-<4-digit number>, for example llm-0001. It is permanent: if the question is retired, its id is not reused.

version.description: Goes up when the stem, the options or the answer change, so statistics from different versions are not mixed.

area.description: Id of an area in taxonomy.json.

subtopic.description: Id of a subtopic of that area in taxonomy.json.

level.description: easy: remember or understand. medium: apply, compare or calculate. hard: analyze or evaluate; never just recall something niche.

bloom.description: The cognitive process the question requires, following the revised Bloom's taxonomy (Anderson and Krathwohl, 2001). 'Create' is left out because a multiple-choice question cannot assess it.

type.description: concept: a definition or a mechanism. scenario: a case with constraints and a best decision. calculation: a short calculation. code: read or fix code. evidence: an answer backed by a cited experimental result.

format.description: single: one correct option. multiple: mark every correct option.

stability.description: stable: does not change (math, papers, definitions). slow: changes over years (good practices). volatile: changes over months (tools, products, new phenomena).

difficulty.description: Up-front difficulty rubric. Each criterion goes from 0 to 2 and is added to the Bloom score (remember and understand 0, apply 1, analyze and evaluate 2). The sum (0 to 8) suggests the level: 0–2 easy, 3–5 medium, 6–8 hard.

steps.description: Reasoning steps to the answer. 0: one. 1: two or three. 2: four or more.

specialization.description: 0: covered in any introductory course. 1: learned by working in the field. 2: niche or research.

distractors.description: 0: easy to rule out. 1: one is plausible. 2: several match common mistakes.

keep_order.description: true if the options have a natural order (numbers, steps). The site shows them in the written order instead of shuffling them.

answer.description: Ids of the correct options. Unless keep_order is set, the site shuffles the options when showing them.

collection.description: Groups questions from the same source, for example strange-machines.

origin.description: Only human and llm_reviewed are published. llm_draft is a generated draft that nobody has reviewed.

review_by.description: Deadline for the next review. Required if the stability is slow or volatile.

rationale.description: Why this option is right or wrong. It is shown after answering.
